sienna: Hey team — quick Q. I'm planning a 3-month stint in Portugal (May 15 - Aug 15) while my partner has a sabbatical. Do I need to do anything for the WFH stipend, benefits, or taxes? :wave:

marco-peopleops: Short answer: yes on a couple of admin items, but this is generally doable for 3 months. Can you confirm exact dates and whether you'll keep US as your home base/address? :eyes:

sienna: Dates above. I'll keep my US address as primary, but will have a temporary Airbnb in Porto. No local employer in Portugal or pay there — still on Redwood payroll in USD.

dan-payroll: Thanks for the heads up, @sienna. For payroll/tax we usually treat short-term remote (<6 months) as permitted, but we need you to file the short-term remote form and provide travel dates. A couple quick notes:
- US tax withholding continues as normal for US citizens/residents.
- Portugal tax residency typically uses the 183-day rule, so 3 months should not trigger automatic residency.
- However, employer presence and local social security rules can be nuanced; we need to confirm there is no local permanent establishment or payroll obligation for this time window.

sienna: Got it — where's the form?

people-ops-bot: Hey! Submit the short-term remote request here: https://intranet.redwood/work-from-abroad and attach: passport copy, travel itinerary, temporary address, and expected return date. People Ops will review within 3 business days. :white_check_mark:

marco-peopleops: Also — WFH stipend: stipend is paid monthly and will be prorated based on days in the month where you're working abroad. If you want the stipend paid to your usual US bank account, we'll keep the default. If you want local currency, let us know and payroll will advise on FX and banking.

emily-hr: Benefits note: short-term travel under 6 months typically keeps you on Redwood benefits (medical, dental) as long as you're still an active employee and maintain your enrollment. However, provider networks and out-of-country coverage vary — please review the international care guidance in benefits docs and consider travel medical insurance for routine care.

sarah-legal: Quick legal flag: confirm you won't be performing any client-facing activities or negotiating contracts while in Portugal. That helps reduce legal risk around permanent establishment. Also provide project list if you'll be doing sales/BD work. For full compliance we might need a simple attestation from you.

marco-peopleops: To summarize action items for @sienna:
1) Fill short-term remote form and attach docs (people-ops-bot link).
2) Tell us preferred stipend payout (US bank or local).
3) Confirm no client-facing/contract work (reply here).
4) Payroll will confirm there is no local payroll obligation.

sienna: I mainly have individual IC work — code and product, no client meetings. Stipend to US bank is fine. Filling the form now. Thanks! :thumbsup:

dan-payroll: Received — once the form is in we'll do a quick check with our EU tax consultant (timeline ~2 business days). If anything changes (stay extends >183 days or you take local contracts), we'll re-evaluate.

people-ops-bot: Checklist submitted: short-term remote form RECEIVED. Review in progress.

emily-hr: One more: if you expect to be offline due to travel/phone number change, please update your contact method in AD and add an out-of-office to calendar.

sienna: Will do. Appreciate the quick help everyone.

marco-peopleops: Happy to help — ping here if legal/payroll have follow-ups. Safe travels! :airplane:
